name: @role-orchestrator/scm-contracts
description: M7-01 controlled GitHub/GitLab integration contracts (DESIGN ONLY - no live provider is contacted). Defines the unified SCMProvider surface with a hard read/write separation that holds as both a static-type fact and a runtime fact: the read-only client type and its read-transport dependency have NO write methods, and every controlled write call refuses without an ApprovalRef (typed ScmApprovalRequiredError). Remote writes reuse @role-orchestrator/approval's actionDigest single-consumption semantics (A17 by analogy): the complete write command (provider, operation, repo, subject, branches, content hashes, plus the run binding: runtime/profileRevision/paths/SHAs/permissions) is hashed into the descriptor, so changing ANY element after approval - including the target PR/issue/SHA - recomputes a different digest and the original approval becomes unconsumable; consumption is the real guarded CAS via approval's lifecycle. Credentials exist ONLY as ScmCredentialRef (env var / keyring entry / file path references that structurally reject plaintext token shapes) and as an opaque, secret-free ResolvedCredentialHandle; receipts and audit events carry content digests, never content or credentials, and a token-shape scrubber provides defense in depth (A42). A per-provider compatibility matrix ships with every verification cell pinned to status literal 'unverified' (the schema cannot express 'verified'), so by default NO client - read or write - can even be constructed: real GitHub/GitLab integration stays fail-closed OFF until a future task flips cells with evidence.
